tagline: From La Cañada Flintridge to nearly 8,000 feet, the long way.
intro: Out of La Cañada Flintridge, at about 1,300 feet, the Angeles Crest Highway turns north into the San Gabriel Mountains and keeps climbing. Between there and Wrightwood there is little built along it but campgrounds, visitor centers and Newcomb's Ranch. At Dawson Saddle it tops out near 7,900 feet, then winds east through switchbacks and blind curves and comes down by Big Pines toward Wrightwood.

Work began in 1929 on what was meant as a fire access road, built with prison labor from Camp 37. The war stopped it in 1941, and it opened in 1956. A freeway was planned up here in the 1950s. The plan was dropped as geographically improbable.

moments.title: Red Box
moments.text: At this 4,665-foot saddle the Mount Wilson road turns off, 4.5 miles up to the observatory whose 100-inch Hooker telescope had the largest aperture in the world from 1917 to 1949.

moments.title: Islip Saddle
moments.text: The Pacific Crest Trail crosses the highway at this pass, named for the homesteader George Islip, and a gate just east of the parking lot shuts the road to Vincent Gap in winter.

moments.title: Big Pines
moments.text: Los Angeles County built a year-round recreation area here in 1924. It is the highest settlement on the San Andreas Fault, with a sag pond, Jackson Lake, just to the west.

practical: The stretch between Islip Saddle and Vincent Gap is generally closed from mid-December to mid-May for snow and rockfall.
